description: The size of each funding source is measured by how many distinct projects it has spatial data for.

b.request: For each funding source (treating missing values as a separate group), count distinct projects appearing in scanspatial records; calculate the average boxy/boxz ratio per source ignoring missing values; identify sources with above-average project counts; output one row with their combined project count, average of their boxy/boxz ratios, and the mean per-source excess above the overall mean project count.
b.sql:
WITH funding_project_stats AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(p.fundflux, 'NULL') as funding_source,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ss.arcref) as project_count,
    AVG(CASE WHEN ss.boxy IS NOT NULL AND ss.boxz IS NOT NULL AND ss.boxz <> 0 THEN ss.boxy / ss.boxz ELSE NULL END) as avg_ratio
  FROM scanspatial ss
  LEFT JOIN projects p ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry
  GROUP BY COALESCE(p.fundflux, 'NULL')
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(project_count) as overall_avg_project_count
  FROM funding_project_stats
),
above_average_sources AS (
  SELECT
    fps.project_count,
    fps.avg_ratio,
    fps.project_count - os.overall_avg_project_count as excess
  FROM funding_project_stats fps
  CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
  WHERE fps.project_count > os.overall_avg_project_count
)
SELECT
  SUM(project_count) as combined_project_count,
  AVG(avg_ratio) as average_of_boxy_boxz_ratios,
  AVG(excess) as mean_per_source_excess
FROM above_average_sources;

c.request: Looking at spatial scan data (`scanspatial`) linked to projects (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), which funding sources (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) are bigger than average? For each funding source, work out the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and how big it is. For the sources above the average size across funding sources, give one row with the average of their ratios, their combined size, and how far on average they exceed the average size. No rounding. The size of each funding source is measured by how many distinct projects it has spatial data for.
c.sql: WITH funding_stats AS (SELECT COALESCE(p.fundflux, 'Missing') as funding_source, COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) as project_count, AVG(CASE WHEN ss.boxy IS NOT NULL AND ss.boxz IS NOT NULL AND ss.boxz != 0 THEN ss.boxy / ss.boxz ELSE NULL END) as avg_ratio FROM scanspatial ss JOIN projects p ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry GROUP BY COALESCE(p.fundflux, 'Missing')), overall_stats AS (SELECT AVG(project_count) as avg_count FROM funding_stats), above_avg AS (SELECT fs.avg_ratio, fs.project_count, os.avg_count FROM funding_stats fs, overall_stats os WHERE fs.project_count > os.avg_count) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) as average_of_ratios, SUM(project_count) as combined_size, AVG(project_count - avg_count) as avg_excess FROM above_avg

a.request: Using spatial records (`scanspatial`) matched to a project (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), for each funding source (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) compute the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and the number of distinct projects. Keep the funding sources whose number of distinct projects is above the average of that number across all funding sources. Return one row with: the average of the kept sources' ratios; the total of their distinct project counts; and the average amount by which their counts exceed the cross-source average. No rounding.
a.sql:
WITH funding_stats AS (
  SELECT
    p.fundflux,
    AVG(ss.boxy / ss.boxz) as avg_ratio,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ss.arcref) as distinct_projects
  FROM scanspatial ss
  JOIN projects p ON ss.arcref = p.arcregistry
  WHERE ss.boxy IS NOT NULL AND ss.boxz IS NOT NULL AND ss.boxz != 0
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
avg_project_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(distinct_projects) as avg_count
  FROM funding_stats
),
kept_sources AS (
  SELECT
    fs.avg_ratio,
    fs.distinct_projects,
    apc.avg_count
  FROM funding_stats fs
  CROSS JOIN avg_project_count apc
  WHERE fs.distinct_projects > apc.avg_count
)
SELECT
  AVG(ks.avg_ratio),
  SUM(ks.distinct_projects),
  AVG(ks.distinct_projects - ks.avg_count)
FROM kept_sources ks

d.request: For each funding source (including NULL as a separate group), measure size as the count of distinct projects with spatial data, calculate the average bounding box Y-to-Z ratio per source, identify sources with above-average project count, and return one row with the average of their ratios, combined project count, and average excess over mean project count.
d.sql:
WITH project_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    p.fundflux,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) as project_count,
    AVG(ss.boxy / ss.boxz) as avg_ratio
  FROM projects p
  INNER JOIN scanspatial ss ON p.arcregistry = ss.arcref
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
mean_calculation AS (
  SELECT AVG(project_count) as mean_count
  FROM project_stats
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT 
    ps.project_count,
    ps.avg_ratio,
    mc.mean_count
  FROM project_stats ps
  CROSS JOIN mean_calculation mc
  WHERE ps.project_count > mc.mean_count
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_ratio) as average_ratio,
  SUM(project_count) as combined_project_count,
  AVG(project_count - mean_count) as average_excess
FROM above_average
